cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Stay for the Hard Part
cards.instruction: Create increasing moments of emotional honesty to test whether someone remains present and supportive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I haven't booked our anniversary trip. Can you hear why before you get your laptop?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought you just needed help with the flights.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I let you think that. I was relieved when the cheap seats sold out.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll leave the laptop shut. Is it the trip, or us?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Us. I hoped a cancellation would say it for me. Can you still sit beside me while I explain?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 rank prefixes do not alter the vulnerable can-you-hear and A5 can-you-sit requests; the actual honesty test is not shaped by superior permission.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 practical-flight assumption causes A3 admission of relief; B4 laptop-shut support and direct question cause A5 relationship disclosure.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers practical help and B4 puts it aside to hear the real issue, actively supporting the increasing honesty.

heightening.evidence: B4 trip-or-us distinction causes A5 more consequential truth and a renewed presence request.

specificity.evidence: A1 anniversary booking and A3 sold-out relief establish avoidance; A5 us makes the emotional issue clear without its full details.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 hoped cancellation would speak is specific but earnest, with stock hierarchy language jarring.

coach2.inferred: A is becoming more honest, not continuing to conceal the problem.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 explains the practical help assumed from A1 request.
